chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Musadif, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who prayed an obligatory prayer while his hair was curled, he said: He should repeat his prayer.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man's prayer if his hair is curled?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that a man whose hair is curled (*mu'qass*) must repeat his obligatory prayer, indicating that this specific grooming style was considered a defect or impurity affecting the completeness of the ritual. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and physical presentation during worship, where certain aesthetic states were historically viewed as detracting from the solemnity of *Salat*. The requirement to repeat the prayer underscores the distinction between mere validity (*sahih*) and the preferred completeness (*kamal*) of the act in Shia jurisprudence.
